text:
Jordan - Product: Quick PRD sketch for the kernel/kv changes we promised AtlasPay. High level: (1) opt-in quantized kernel variant for large-chat models, (2) KV cache TTL/eviction policy with explicit canary + fallback, (3) rollout gates tied to customer latency SLO and a small prompt-set quality check. Need engineering acceptance criteria and a realistic launch checklist.

Anya (Eng Runtime): copying the gist here. Are we requiring model-bit-compatibility testing as part of the canary?

Jordan - Product: yes — we need compatibility + quality smoke. Mira, what did AtlasPay say about error/burst tolerance?

Mira (Customer Success): they care most about tail latency and deterministic fallbacks. If quant kernel increases hallucination even slightly it's a blocker. They asked for a canary on 5% traffic for 2 weeks and automatic fallback to FP16 on error.

Sam G: for rollout policy we should define exact metrics and thresholds. Suggest: p95 latency <= 250ms, error rate delta <= 0.1% absolute, quality regression measured by automated prompt-set A/B with BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies + manual spot checks.

Vikram (SRE): plus infra constraints: if KV cache hit rate < 60% under canary load we shouldn't enable the reduced-KV-size path. Also need evictions to be observable + traces to show cache miss spikes.

Anya (Eng Runtime): drafting acceptance criteria: 
- Functional: quant kernel returns numerically compatible logits (within tolerance) for sample suite.
- Quality: no >1.5% absolute regression on regression suite on canary traffic.
- Latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.20 and absolute p95 <= 250ms.
- Reliability: fallback to previous kernel within 30s of detection, rollback auto if error delta > 0.2%.
- Observability: metrics + traces emitted for kernel selection, kv_hit_rate, kv_evictions, fallback_count.

Anya (Eng Runtime): edge cases to call out: sequence-length spikes, cold-start KV miss storms, concurrent model-version pinning from Dedicated customers, and mixed-quant-precision client requests.

Jordan - Product: good list. For rollout gates we want a small canary (5%), then 25% ramp for 48h, then 100% if green. Include a manual hold for customer-initiated canary extension.

Mira (Customer Success): AtlasPay will request canary visibility. Can we expose a per-customer dashboard for kernel variant & kv stats?

Sam G: yes but scoped: read-only dashboard with p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, fallback_count, and a link to failing prompts. Implementation note: we can reuse existing per-route dashboards and add a kernel_variant tag.

Vikram (SRE): rollout config snippet suggestion (for ops):
```yaml
canary: 0.05
steps:
  - to: 0.25
    duration: 48h
  - to: 1.0
    duration: 24h
rules:
  - metric: p95_latency
    threshold: 250ms
    action: rollback
  - metric: quality_regression
    threshold: 1.5%
    action: hold
```

Anya (Eng Runtime): technical questions: 1) Do we require explicit serialization format for cached KV entries between FP16/quant variants? 2) How should we tag cache entries for LRU eviction compatibility?

Jordan - Product: prefer a neutral on-disk/cross-kernel serialization (protobuf v2) and include a version tag. If format mismatch, fallback to repopulate rather than silently misusing.

Sam G: add acceptance test: simulate format mismatch and verify no corruption + successful repopulation within 5s for 95% of cases.

Mira (Customer Success): also add rollback playbook steps we can share with AtlasPay: what to expect, who to paging, and customer-facing message template.

Anya (Eng Runtime): i'll assemble an RFC with: PRD link, acceptance criteria above, rollout YAML, test plan, and rollback playbook. Please review before EOD Thursday.

Jordan - Product: timeline ask — target canary start in 3 weeks. Is that feasible?

Sam G: 3 weeks is tight but doable if kernel builds and infra flags are ready. Need 1 week for test harness & canary dashboard setup.

Vikram (SRE): we need a short maintenance window for the canary start to ensure cluster capacity for the extra variant. Call this out in the RFC.

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance window created: 2026-04-05T02:00:00Z — notify if you want different time.

Jordan - Product: thanks all. Action items: Anya to post RFC, Sam to prep test harness, Vikram to reserve infra & dashboard, Mira to prepare customer playbook and confirm AtlasPay sign-off. We'll reconvene after RFC comments. :raised_hands:
